title: service-proxy-mirroring-nlb-to-alb-canary-upgrade-terraform-module
creator: Diego Ramirez
description:
Problem statement:

Private/VPC deployments currently use a mix of ad-hoc Terraform snippets to wire internal NLBs to ALBs for service ingress. This has led to inconsistent TLS termination behavior, fragile health checks for gRPC services, and no safe way to validate new runtime builds during upgrades without risk to production traffic.

Goal:
Develop a reusable Terraform module that standardizes internal ingress topology (NLB fronting ALB where appropriate), provides first-class TLS termination at the ALB using ACM certificates (with rotation-friendly outputs), supports gRPC and HTTP/1.1 health checks, and introduces a traffic-mirroring + canary traffic routing pattern for safe upgrades in Private deployments. The module should be opinionated but configurable to support: cross-account endpoints, path- and host-based routing, sticky sessions toggle, and explicit health-check policies.

Scope / deliverables:
- New Terraform module under terraform/modules/internal-service-proxy that composes NLB and ALB when customers prefer pre-TLS pass-through + central TLS termination.
- Inputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids, service_port_mapping, target_group_config (protocol, port, healthcheck settings), tls_certificate_arn (optional), mirror_target_arn (optional), canary_weight_percent, enable_stickiness, tags.
acceptance_criteria: Module publishes example usage in README with sample variables for a gRPC backend and an HTTP backend
ALB created with ACM cert attached when tls_certificate_arn provided; otherwise TLS passthrough from NLB to targets
Health checks for gRPC use grpc-specific matcher and support healthy/unhealthy thresholds configurable
Traffic mirroring configuration available: mirror <-> primary target groups with configurable sampling rate
Canary routing supported via weight-based target groups and integrates with Redwood Console rollout hooks (webhook URL output)
Module outputs include load_balancer_dns, listener_arns, target_group_arns, cert_rotation_hint, and generated_tags
Automated acceptance tests (Terratest) validate create/update/destroy flow in a non-prod account
Documentation includes runbook for certificate rotation, healthcheck tuning, and rollback guidance
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha: Initial design spike completed. Prototype demonstrates NLB TCP passthrough + ALB TLS termination anchored by an intermediary EC2 proxy in a PoC; decided to avoid proxy by leveraging NLB TLS passthrough + ALB for advanced routing where customers need host/path rules.

2025-01-20 - Diego: RFC posted in Confluence (link below). Main trade-offs discussed: single ALB per service vs shared ALB with host-based routing. We chose single logical ALB per logical service for predictable routing and certificate scoping.

2025-01-28 - Engineering review: Feedback from infra team to surface an option for client-side IP preservation for telemetry. Added support for X-Forwarded-For preservation and proxy-protocol toggles on NLB listeners.
2025-02-05 - Security review kickoff: requested threat model for TLS termination and cross-account access. Pending IAM scoped role design for cross-account target registration.

2025-02-10 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/142 - contains module v0.1. Included Terratest harness and example usage files. CI failing on cleanup in us-west-2 sandbox due to race in target group deregistration.

2025-02-15 - Aisha: Fixed deregistration race in PR, added backoff and explicit deregistration wait. Began adding Console rollout webhook output and sample alert rule for unhealthy target rate >5% over 5m.

Next steps: finish security IAM role for cross-account, run terratest in staging, request SOC review, enable canary rollout integration with Console via webhook and add Dashboard widgets for mirrored traffic and canary error delta.
